acceptance: get_instructions, the todo://instructions resource, the todo/workflow prompt and the initialize handshake instructions include a 'Bound store' section naming the state remote with any credentials removed, the branch, how the target was resolved (flag, env, config file path or discovery) and the worker identity; tests assert the section for each resolution source

get_instructions accepts an optional expect_store text; when it does not occur, case-insensitively, in the redacted remote#branch the call returns a gate-kind E_STATE error naming the expected and actual store, and a test covers match and mismatch
The startup log line and every other message that prints the remote use the same credential removal, with a test using a URL that carries a user and token
README and the instructions text tell agents to pass the project's repository name as expect_store on the first call; the tool schema snapshot is regenerated and the CHANGELOG records the change
The todo skill text lives in the external skill-sync-skills catalog, so the matching wording change is reported to the owner, not made in this repository

REVIEW 2026-10-28 against todo-db 0.10.1 (main d85cdf3), per the todo review checklist and review-protocol L2/L3. VERDICT: VALID and required (high). Verified: the bound store is only logged by src/todo_db/mcp/server.py _lifespan, and that log prints state_ref.remote unredacted, so a URL with embedded credentials would reach stderr; no tool, resource or prompt reports it (resources.py returns the static INSTRUCTIONS constant). NARROWED (solution fit): the original acceptance asked for the store in every acknowledgement and list/show response and for a client-supplied expected store on mutations. That is dropped as larger than needed: get_instructions is the documented first call, a mismatch check on that call makes the comparison mechanical instead of relying on the agent noticing, and per-response fields add bytes to every ack and break frozen schemas for no extra detection. Killed with that reason, not re-homed. Residual gap accepted: a client that passes --actor never needs get_instructions, so it can skip the check; the todo skill text covers that by telling agents to call it first.
description: todo-db-mcp resolves its state branch once at launch from flags, then environment, then a .todo-db/config.json found by walking up from the server's working directory, and logs the result only to its own stderr (src/todo_db/mcp/server.py _lifespan, 'target: <remote>#<branch>'). No tool response, get_instructions text or acknowledgement names it. An agent therefore cannot tell which tracker it is writing to, and a server started from the wrong directory writes to the wrong tracker without any error. This happened: a session whose working directory was the todo-db repository, using the repo's .mcp.json (command todo-db-mcp, no args, no env), created, claimed, edited and finished 15 BenchBox work items in joeharris76/todo-db's todo-state branch (110 items) instead of BenchBox-dev/BenchBox's (3,875 items). The CLI, run from the BenchBox checkout, correctly reported 'unknown task'; the agent treated the MCP as authoritative and dismissed it. A different BenchBox session later created its own sqlglot-overlay-vacuous-guard record in the right tracker, so the item now exists in both with different histories.
